purpose: Define how each public contract evolves. Without this, a small contract set is a promise with no mechanism — and the one contract whose artifacts live in user repositories has no upgrade path.

decisionDependencies.claim: structure is governed by a small set of public versioned contracts, not a package count
the recipe is versioned independently of the fact schema; skipped releases must not mass-invalidate
consumers pin a schema major and receive a typed refusal rather than a reshaped document
physical storage schema is private and freely migratable
exit classes are a public contract with executable goldens
decisionDependencies.direction: VERSIONING depends on D9 for the additive-only exit-class rule (V4). D9 does NOT depend on VERSIONING.
decisionDependencies.note: B-SCV2-06: v1 cited D9 v1.4 while scope-correction v2 asserted D9 depends on VERSIONING, making ownership circular or hidden. The direction is now declared and VER-DEP checks the citation resolves to the live binding artifact.

principle.core: A contract's evolution policy is determined by WHO HOLDS ITS ARTIFACTS, not by how important it feels.
principle.rationale: If the artifacts live only in our release, a breaking change costs a version bump. If they live in user repositories, a breaking change costs every user a migration they did not ask for — and if it happens silently, it costs their trust in the gate. These are different problems and cannot share one policy.
principle.consequence: Contracts are classified by artifact custody, and the custody class dictates the mechanism.

custodyClasses.meaning: Artifacts are created by the tool and stored in the user's repository, under their version control, outliving any release.

policy.breakingChange: Requires a migrator, not a major bump alone.
policy.support: Last K majors readable, K >= 2, published as a number not a vibe.
policy.negotiation: Every artifact self-declares the version it was written under. The host reads the declaration; it never infers from shape.
policy.unsupportedVersion: INDETERMINATE with repair instructions. NEVER a silent re-interpretation and never a mass net-new diff.
policy.migration: Explicit, previewable, and idempotent. `--check` shows the diff without writing.
policy.dualEmit: Where two identities can be computed, emit both during the transition window so a mid-upgrade fleet matches on either.

custodyClasses.why: This is the class that can destroy trust. A user who skipped three releases and comes back to a flood of false net-new findings concludes the gate is unreliable — and they are right to.

custodyClasses.meaning: No stored artifact, but an external consumer's code depends on the shape at runtime — CI scripts, agents, dashboards.

policy.breakingChange: New major, offered alongside the old for a published window.
policy.negotiation: The consumer requests a major explicitly. An unsupported request is a typed refusal, never a best-effort reshape.
policy.additive: New optional fields are minor. A consumer that rejects unknown fields is non-conforming; this must be stated so additive change stays cheap.
policy.exitCodesSpecial: Exit classes may only be ADDED, never renumbered or repurposed. A build script cannot negotiate.

custodyClasses.why: The failure mode is silent: a reshaped document parses, produces a different meaning, and CI does the wrong thing without erroring.

custodyClasses.meaning: Third-party authors compile or validate against it.

policy.breakingChange: New major with an overlap window; contributions declare a supported range and the host refuses outside it at admission, not at first use.
policy.negotiation: Handshake at admission: host advertises supported ranges, contribution declares its requirement, mismatch is an admission rejection with both ranges named.
policy.deprecation: Announce, then warn on use, then refuse. Each stage is a release, not a day.

custodyClasses.why: Cheaper than user-custody because authors can respond to a release; more expensive than internal because they are not us.

custodyClasses.meaning: No external party depends on the shape.

policy.requirement: Anything derived must be REBUILDABLE from retained inputs, or it is not internal — it is evidence, and evidence is user-custody.
policy.test: If deleting it loses information a retained Run needs, it was misclassified.

custodyClasses.why: The whole point of keeping storage private is to be able to change it. If internal layouts acquire external dependents, that freedom is lost silently.

versionedIdentities.note: Not itself a contract; the vehicle.
Family distinguishes this contract from any predecessor with a colliding version number.
Independent of the fact schema — that independence is the whole reason it exists.
Relation-level granularity so adding a relation does not break rules that never used it.

rules.rule: Every public contract declares exactly one custody class. Unclassified means unshippable.
A USER-CUSTODY breaking change without a migrator is prohibited, regardless of how the version is numbered.
No consumer-facing document is reshaped in place. Either the consumer's requested major is served, or the request is refused with the supported range named.
Exit classes are additive-only, forever. Renumbering silently changes the meaning of every CI configuration in existence.
Compatibility is negotiated at admission, not discovered at first use. A contribution incompatible with the host fails to load with both ranges reported.
Support windows are published as concrete counts and dates. 'We support recent versions' is not a policy.
Anything reachable from a retained Run is USER-CUSTODY by definition, whatever it was labelled. Custody follows reachability, not intent.

A version identity that participates in PlanId cannot change without changing derived identity — so bumping it invalidates caches by construction. This is a feature; do not add compatibility shims that hide it.

Any change that makes a byte sequence reachable from a retained Run is a VERSIONING REVIEW EVENT. Reachability is checked mechanically: the evidence reachability graph must never point at a path the inventory labels INTERNAL.
rules.why: V7 says custody follows reachability, which means custody can change SILENTLY — a refactor that starts embedding an internal structure in a Run has just made it USER-CUSTODY without anyone deciding to. A1-VER-03.

conformanceTests.assert: Every public contract declares exactly one custody class; an unclassified contract fails the release gate.
A USER-CUSTODY breaking change without a SPECIFIED migrator is refused by the release gate.
conformanceTests.note: A1-VER-01: this was vacuous in v1 because no migrator existed for any member. Four are now specified; run-manifest is NOT-YET-ENFORCEABLE and is excluded from discharge.

conformanceTests.assert: A consumer requesting an unsupported major receives a typed refusal naming the supported range, never a reshaped document.
Exit classes can be added but never renumbered or repurposed.
A contribution incompatible with the host fails to load at admission with both ranges reported.
Every migrator runs offline from in-release code and fetches nothing.
`--check` previews a migration without writing, and running a migrator twice is a no-op.
A baseline comparison across a detector change classifies each difference as CODE-NET-NEW, DETECTION-DELTA, or CODE-FIXED using the detector pivot.
When the pivot detector is unavailable the comparison reports INDETERMINATE for it and never attributes the delta to code.
A waiver whose target identity changes under migration is reported individually, never summarised.
The evidence reachability graph never points at a path the inventory labels INTERNAL.

peerReviewRequired: Is the detector pivot affordable? It requires running the OLD detector over new code on every comparison that crosses a detector version — potentially doubling analysis cost during a transition window.
Blind re-authoring of the seven comparison fixtures.
A1-VER-05 needs a PRODUCT owner. Every support window is a guess and may stay one.
knownLimitations: Every support window is GUESSED and the corresponding property is NOT DISCHARGED. VT-12's harness may be unbuildable by design.
The detector pivot doubles work during a transition window; no measurement supports the claim that this is affordable.
The run-manifest migrator is NOT-YET-ENFORCEABLE, so evidence bundles are USER-CUSTODY by V7 with no migration path.

migrators.why: A1-VER-01: V2 forbids a USER-CUSTODY breaking change without a migrator, and v1 specified no migrator for any member. A prohibition with no named mechanism is vacuous, and it was discharging a sealed property.

airGap.rule: A migrator SHIPS IN THE RELEASE. It may not fetch anything.
airGap.consequence: If a transition genuinely needs data not present locally, it is NOT a migrator — it is a re-analysis, and it must be reported as such rather than disguised as an upgrade.
airGap.why: The air-gap posture and the migrator obligation collide the moment a migrator needs the network. Resolving it in favour of in-release packaging keeps both promises; resolving it the other way would quietly break air-gap for exactly the users who care most.

migrators.rule: A USER-CUSTODY member with no SPECIFIED migrator may not undergo a breaking change, whatever the version number says.

detectorSemanticDelta.why: B-CSG-04 / CS-04. Exact artifact identity detects that a baseline comparison changed; it CANNOT say whether the change is new code, a changed detector, or the user adopting a new level. All three look like net-new findings, and treating a detector improvement as a regression is how a guardrail loses its users.
detectorSemanticDelta.theProblem: A two-way diff compares (code0, detector0) against (code1, detector1) and attributes the whole difference to code. Two variables moved; one difference was measured.

theFix.name: three-way comparison with a detector pivot
theFix.pivot: Run detector0 over code1. Call the result P.

decomposition.meaning: the same detector, applied to new code, finds something new. This is a real regression.
the detector changed its mind about unchanged code. Not a regression.
the same detector no longer fires — genuine improvement.

theFix.requires: detector0 must still be RUNNABLE. That is exactly what the dual-emit window in the custody policy provides, which is the real reason dual-emit exists: not merely to soften churn, but to make this classification computable at all.

ifPivotUnavailable.rule: The comparison reports which detectors could not be pivoted and why. It NEVER falls back to attributing the whole delta to code.
ifPivotUnavailable.why: Silently attributing a detection delta to the user's code is a false net-new finding presented as a regression — the trust-destroying failure the custody class exists to prevent.

theFix.adoption: A user opting into a new normalisation level or a new rule set is a THIRD case, and it is not inferred: it is an explicit acceptance recorded in the transition, so it never enters the diff as either of the two above.

detectorSemanticDelta.relationToFactIdentity: fact-identity-policy's custody transition protocol supplies the dual-emit window and the many-to-many group mapping this comparison consumes. The two contracts are the same mechanism seen from the baseline side and the identity side.

shipGate.rule: Dual-emit / detector-pivot path MUST NOT ship as the default gate-compare behaviour without either: (a) product acceptance of a documented cost bound (including potential ~2× analysis during multi-major support), or (b) an optimization that keeps pivot off the hot path (cache pivot results; pivot only on detector major change when baseline compare is requested — not on every analysis). Affordability is UNMEASURED; silence is not acceptance (R1-VER-01).
shipGate.defaultUntilDisposition: Pivot runs only when: detector major changes AND a baseline/gate-compare is explicitly requested. Ordinary analysis without compare does not invoke the pivot.
shipGate.forbids: Claiming the pivot is cheap or free; skipping pivot silently and attributing DETECTION-DELTA as CODE-NET-NEW

detectorSemanticDelta.costHonesty: knownLimitations: pivot doubles work during transition. Do not claim affordability without measurement. Correct classification is necessary; unbounded CI cost without disposition makes operators skip pivot and reintroduce false regressions (R1-VER-01).

agentProtocolNote.position: The agent protocol surface is CONSUMER-CUSTODY for shape, but its negotiation is SESSION-SCOPED: a client advertises the major it wants at connect and is refused if unsupported.
agentProtocolNote.consequence: No multi-release dual-serve obligation is incurred for agents alone. A durable agent runtime that outlives a session would change this, and none exists.
agentProtocolNote.why: Dual-serving every major for a surface whose consumers reconnect every session is cost with no beneficiary.

dischargeStatus.rule: A property may be SPECIFIED by an implementable test declaration. It may be DISCHARGED only at the canonical DEMONSTRATED state: retained evidence that the test ran against its required domain and its negative controls failed. implementable:true alone is NOT discharge (R2-FINAL-02).
dischargeStatus.testReferenceSemantics: The legacy dischargedBy key names tests that specify or exercise the property. It is not demonstration evidence and never changes assurance state by itself.

comparisonSchema.why: The classification results and the migrator declaration were referenced throughout and never typed. Two implementations could emit different vocabularies and both claim conformance — the same defect B-FI-09 raised against the normalisation ladder.

classification.rule: Closed. An unknown classification is rejected, not passed through as advisory.

indeterminateReason.rule: REQUIRED when classification is INDETERMINATE. An unexplained indeterminate is indistinguishable from a bug.

MigratorDeclaration.rule: A migrator with status SPECIFIED and any missing field is a release-gate failure, not a warning.

comparisonSchema.gateRule: Only CODE-NET-NEW may fail a ratchet gate. DETECTION-DELTA and INDETERMINATE are reported and never gate, because neither is evidence the user regressed.
